title: Zoltan Hyacinth, killed in altercation with police, subject of inquest
subtitle: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit cleared officers of wrongdoing in case
article: The Ontario government will hold an inquest into the death of Zoltan Hyacinth, a 23-year-old who died of a gunshot wound during an altercation with Toronto police.
Hyacinth died on the evening of March 17, 2013, as police tried to arrest him at a Burger King in the Keele Street and Wilson Avenue area.
Ontario's Special Investigations Unit, which probes all incidents involving police when death or serious injury occur, cleared the officers of wrongdoing in the case.

According to the SIU's investigation, Hyacinth suffered a fatal gunshot wound after police officers boxed in his car then pulled him from the vehicle. As the officers struggled, a gun allegedly belonging to Hyacinth, was fired three times.

"Hyacinth discharged the gun three times in quick succession as it was pointed in a northerly direction almost parallel to the ground, presumably in an attempt to shoot one or more officers involved in his arrest. Instead of effecting his purpose, he shot himself in the head, causing his own demise," the SIU's report said.
Hyacinth was pronounced dead at the scene.
In the wake of the shooting, Michelle Hyacinth, Zoltan's mother, told CBC News that she didn't believe her son had shot himself and didn't think he had a gun.
"I know that's a lie," she said, adding she always searched her son's room.

A Ruger semi-automatic pistol was recovered at the scene, the SIU investigation said, and forensic testing matched it to the bullets fired. The police present during the arrest were armed with Glock handguns.
The inquest is set to begin on Oct. 5 and is expected to hear from about 20 witnesses.
In announcing the inquest, the province noted an inquest is mandatory under the Coroners Act.
